concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: In which year did the English East India Company pass a new law that required every new person who took up employment in the Company’s army to serve overseas if required?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1856**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In **1856**, the English East India Company passed a law mandating that soldiers employed in its army had to serve overseas if required.
 
• This law was significant as it challenged the traditional beliefs of Indian sepoys, particularly regarding crossing the seas, which was considered against their religious practices.
 
• The resentment caused by this law among Indian soldiers contributed to the growing unrest that eventually culminated in the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
• This regulation was part of the larger socio-political changes introduced by the British to consolidate their control over India.
 
• The law showcased the disregard of the British towards local cultural sensitivities, leading to widespread dissatisfaction among Indian troops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• The revolt was triggered by multiple factors, including resentment over policies like the overseas service law and the introduction of Enfield rifles with cartridges rumored to be greased with cow and pig fat.
 
• It is considered the first major uprising against British rule in India.
 
• Both sepoys and civilians participated in the revolt, which started in Meerut and spread across northern and central India.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Sensitivities:**
 
 
• Crossing the seas was considered a religious taboo among certain Indian communities, as it was believed to result in the loss of caste.
 
• The imposition of the overseas service regulation was seen as an affront to traditional values.
 
 
 
• **English East India Company:**
 
 
• The company governed India until 1858, after which control was transferred to the British Crown.
 
• Its policies often ignored local customs, leading to widespread dissatisfaction and resistance among Indians.
 
 
 
• **Military Reforms:**
 
 
• British reforms in the Indian army aimed at aligning the forces with Western military practices.
 
• These reforms were often resisted by Indian soldiers due to cultural and religious differences.
